record.paper_title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.
record.context_brief: Time-like separation of form factors and phase measurement
record.original_question: Can time-like-region measurements in e+e− annihilation or proton-antiproton reactions separately determine the electric and magnetic proton and neutron form factors, and can time-like polarization observables such as A_y and A_xz, which contain respectively the imaginary and real parts of G_E G_M*, determine the relative phase between the complex time-like electric and magnetic form factors?

evidence.quote: No polarization experiment has been done in TL region.
In TL region, polarization data allow to access the phase of FFs.
In order to determine the relative phase of FFs, in TL region, the interesting observables are Ay, and Axz which contain, respectively, the imaginary and the real part of the product GEG∗M.
But even larger progress is expected in the TL region, where data are scarce and no individual determination of the two nucleon FFs has been done yet.

In particular new data on the neutron are expected in Frascati, as well as polarization experiments which will allow to determine firstly the relative phase between the complex electric and magnetic FFs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon (proton and neutron), defined through the matrix element of the electromagnetic current between nucleon states and parametrized by the Sachs electric and magnetic form factors G_E(q^2) and G_M(q^2). In the space-like region (q^2 < 0) these are real functions of q^2, while in the time-like region (q^2 > 0, accessible through reactions such as e^+ e^- → N \bar N or \bar p p → e^+ e^-) they are complex analytic functions and acquire a relative phase.

(a) Devise an experimental and theoretical procedure based on time-like measurements in e^+ e^- annihilation and/or proton–antiproton reactions that separately determines |G_E^p|, |G_M^p|, |G_E^n|, |G_M^n| as functions of q^2, rather than only effective combinations.

(b) Show that the single-spin polarization observable A_y (the analyzing power normal to the scattering plane) and the double-spin observable A_xz are proportional, respectively, to Im(G_E G_M^*) and Re(G_E G_M^*) in the time-like region, and use these observables to determine the relative phase between G_E(q^2) and G_M(q^2) as a complex function of q^2 above threshold.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent measurements at BaBar, BESIII, and CMD-3 have achieved separation of |G_E| and |G_M| for the proton in the time-like region via the proton helicity angular distribution, and the ratio |G_E/G_M| has been extracted at several q^2 values. Relative phase measurements between G_E and G_M for baryons in the time-like region have also been reported recently. However, individual separation of the neutron G_E and G_M and a full mapping of the relative phase remain incomplete, so the program is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of proton electromagnetic form factors in the time-like region using initial state radiation at BESIII
status_evidence.snippet: The ratio |G_E/G_M| and the values of |G_eff|, |G_E|, |G_M| are measured by studying the helicity angle of the proton.
status_evidence.claim: Individual proton |G_E| and |G_M| have been separated in the time-like region.

status_evidence.title: Extracting the femtometer structure of strange baryons using the vacuum polarization effect
status_evidence.snippet: It has become possible to measure not only the magnitude of G_E and G_M of baryons, but also their relative phases in the timelike region.
status_evidence.claim: Relative phase measurements between G_E and G_M for baryons in the time-like region have been performed.

status_evidence.title: New fit of timelike proton electromagnetic form factors from colliders
status_evidence.snippet: Data from BaBar, BESIII, and CMD-3 are examined; moduli of the individual form factors are determined for the first time.
status_evidence.claim: Individual time-like proton form factor moduli have been determined from collider data.
